question: What is the earliest documentary point at which Rarámuri color modifiers and their degree semantics can be verified without projecting later analyses backward?

findings: Historical basic color forms occur in -cameke/-gameke, with attested truncations in -came for black, white and green.
Historical stative -ga~-ja is independently analyzed with -(a)meke, and -na is explicitly segmented as a verbalizer in red tsestá-na.
No accessible published Steffel source audited so far gives the later modern semantic labels 'color subido' versus 'color bajo' for specific color morphemes.
chronology.epistemic_limit: Do not assign twentieth-century degree semantics to individual eighteenth-century morphemes unless directly documented.

chronology.source: Donald Burgess, Los colores en tarahumara, Memoria Ra'ítzari--La Palabra, Primer Seminario Sobre Lenguas Habladas en el Estado de Chihuahua, pp. 84-88
chronology.evidence_type: bibliographic metadata only in current audit
findings: The publication exists and predates the 1983 American Ethnologist article.
chronology.epistemic_limit: Full text not recovered in the present audit; no exact morpheme-to-function claim is attributed to the 1981 paper.

chronology.source: Burgess, Kempton & MacLaury, Tarahumara Color Modifiers: Category Structure Presaging Evolutionary Change, American Ethnologist 10:133-149, DOI 10.1525/ae.1983.10.1.02a00080
findings: The abstract states that basic Tarahumara color terms carry obligatory modifiers.
Those modifiers specify the grade of membership of a color stimulus in a color category.
Therefore explicit semantic organization by color modifiers is documentable at the system level by 1983.
chronology.epistemic_limit: Without the complete article, the exact assignments of individual forms such as -ka or -na are not attributed to this source in the current audit.

chronology.source: Compendio básico de la gramática ralámuli
findings: -ka/-ga/-cha are explicitly grouped as color modifiers for 'subido'.
-na is explicitly described as 'se está poniendo/color bajo'.
The mappings are illustrated across multiple color roots and regional varieties.
chronology.epistemic_limit: This establishes a secure latest-by date for the exact morpheme-to-function mapping in an accessible primary source, not necessarily the date of innovation.

chronology.source: Caballero, A grammar of Choguita Rarámuri
findings: Participial -ame is independently described in Choguita.
Choguita lacks /g/ as a phoneme while retaining /k/, supplying a negative control against a pan-Rarámuri synchronous k~g rule.
chronology.epistemic_limit: This source is used for modern grammatical controls rather than for dating the earlier color-degree semantic system.

interpretation: The modern semantic specialization of obligatory color modifiers is explicitly documented by 1983. The current audit can securely map -ka/-ga/-cha and -na to their specific functions only from the accessible 1997 multivariety source. The historical Steffel evidence demonstrates older morphology but does not by itself date the modern degree opposition.
next_tests: Recover the full text of Burgess 1981 to determine whether the specific -ka/-na semantic mapping was already explicit there.
Recover the full 1983 article to verify the exact forms assigned to central versus marginal category membership.
Search pre-1980 Rarámuri texts for actual usage of -kame/-game/-name in color contexts, while separating corpus usage from later analyst semantics.
